item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00190","case1_error":"Treats the doubled two-week vegetable total as a weekly total before adding weekly kale.","case2_error":"Treats the daily round-trip distance as a weekly total, dividing it by five to obtain daily distance.","reason":"Both assign a distance or quantity to the wrong time period, introducing an erroneous time-conversion factor.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00191","case1_error":"Reduces the required rope length by 25% instead of accounting for the reduced usable length of purchased rope.","case2_error":"Omits the first shot's distance and adds the overshoot instead of subtracting it.","reason":"The first incorrectly applies a loss to the required amount; the second incorrectly combines journey segments and overshoot.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00192","case1_error":"Calculates one company's advertising cost but reports it as the combined cost for three companies.","case2_error":"Calculates pages for one person's two copies but omits the factor of nine people.","reason":"Both omit the number of recipients or purchasers when scaling a correctly calculated per-person or per-company quantity.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00193","case1_error":"Uses the original nine T-shirts as the tripling base instead of the three sweaters found.","case2_error":"Gives an unsupported final answer of 37 after correctly describing the calculation yielding five.","reason":"The first uses an incorrect comparison base; the second supplies an incorrect final number without showing an erroneous calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00194","case1_error":"Invents D − 600 = D/3, ignoring that 600 kilometers is half the total distance.","case2_error":"Omits the second day's final nine miles and the entire third day's 35 miles from the total.","reason":"The first constructs an erroneous distance relation; the second leaves required journey segments out of the sum.","judgment":"different"}]}
